actions.action: Push a finger 2-3 inches into the soil to check moisture
Lift the pot to judge whether the soil is waterlogged
Slide the plant out or look at the drainage holes to inspect the roots
Unpot and cut away mushy, brown or smelly roots and stem tissue
Repot into a pot with drainage holes using chunky, well-draining aroid mix or potting mix with perlite or bark
Remove the inner liner or any saucer that holds standing water
Water thoroughly only when the top 2-3 inches are dry
Empty the saucer 10 minutes after watering
Replace the sticky trap with a shallow dish of water to catch gnats
If the soil is bone dry, water more often instead
If the soil is dry, raise humidity with a pebble tray or by grouping plants

reason: The answer correctly identifies soil staying too wet and overwatering but never names the oversized pot; it advises repotting for drainage and watering less, which overlaps with but does not specify the smaller-pot fix, and nothing in it is harmful.
